Redline round 4

Reviewed the whole pull request. Rounds 1 to 3 are already on this PR; this run starts at round 4.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at a70c243 returned 13 candidates: 3 confirmed, 6 for the person, 0 collapsed into findings already reported or settled, 0 already tracked, 4 dropped (refuted, outside the diff or disproportionate).

This round reviewed the whole PR at a70c243 and verified the coverage pass's 13 candidates. The hand commits for round 3 (6ef58a9, with R3-4 as option B) and for R2-5's guard narrowing (a70c243) landed cleanly, so R3-1 to R3-4 are resolved. Two nits are records that did not follow those commits: the guard standard still calls the narrowing pending, and round 3's standards retrospective never landed. The one correctness finding is an edge of the reopen rule, returned to the person: Redline's own `resolved` reply is read back as `decided`, so a wrongly resolved finding can never reopen. No scheduled or queued work applies (this repository has no routes/console.php), and the version moves from main's 0.1.1 to 0.2.0.

### Findings (1 correctness, 2 nit)

- **R4-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `agent-os/specs/2026-11-06-1019-80-review-round-3/shape.md:105` · Round 3's standards retrospective never landed, and its shape.md still records R3-4 as pending
- **R4-2** · nit · low · confirmed · `agent-os/standards/scripts/guard.md:23` · The guard standard still says a skill fork is approved every redline-gh.sh subcommand and the narrowing is pending
- **R4-3** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:1169` · A finding an earlier run resolved is read back as decided, so a candidate that still reproduces it can never reopen · needs a decision

### Resolved from earlier rounds

- **R3-1** The tech stack still calls the code-review skill a candidate second reviewer, and the edited sentence has lost its subject: agent-os/product/tech-stack.md:5 now says the built-in code-review skill is the finder on every whole-PR and fix-diff round since #79, and the sentence has its own subject (6ef58a9).
- **R3-2** The empty-candidates sentence names the wrong remaining work: docs/running.md:54 now says what the reviewer still runs on an empty array: no discovery pass of its own, the scheduled-and-queued, Docs and Version checks, the fix-diff recheck on a later round, and the carry-forward list on a first round that has one (6ef58a9).
- **R3-3** The handled-list header and the knownAs example still say a fixed match is never re-raised, against the R2-1 reopen rule: When the pass ran, the handled-list header carries the reopen exception (workflows/redline-loop.js:1126); the candidates block and agents/redline-reviewer.md (the known-finding check and the knownAs contract) say a reopened finding's knownAs stays empty; the coverage-off header is unchanged (6ef58a9).
- **R3-4** A decided finding whose decision was applied in commits never reopens, and the verifier cannot tell it was fixed: The person chose option B in 6ef58a9: the header (line 1126), the candidates block (line 1169), agents/redline-reviewer.md and docs/running.md step 7 now say a decided finding stays settled whatever its commits, and that a candidate still reproducing one goes under For the person.

### For the person

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:1892` · R3-4 was decided (option B in 6ef58a9), and this still reproduces its remaining point: history() gives each earlier finding describeOutcome's text but not record.outcomeKinds. So within a run, the verifier can only tell a decided outcome (the decision's notes plus 'decided by') from a fixed one ('fixed in <sha> · decided by: redline') by its wording, while the reopen and settle rules now depend on that kind.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:2785` · The handoff's fallback line 'the last one found no correctness bugs' is also posted after a round that did report correctness findings: when the review dial selects none, or when every finding settles with no commit. The sentence and both paths are unchanged from main. Round 2's For the person already asked for the done rule's own wording here.
- `agent-os/specs/2026-11-06-1019-80-review-round-1/redline/round-1-findings.json:1` · The posted handoff's For the person already says the self-hosted relaunch rewrote round 1's findings and review files. What it leaves out: 5e2a42e then committed those rewritten files and handoff.md as round 1's record. The folder now says round 1 found 0 findings, while the posted round 1 review and the reply files beside them list R1-1 to R1-6.
- `agent-os/standards/workflow/replay.md:15` · The new bullet says coverage off keeps every prompt byte-identical to the time before the pass existed. But the findings file built in post() (workflows/redline-loop.js:2141) now always carries "forThePerson": [], so every `post r<n>` prompt differs from 0.1.x. Harmless within a run, since has-review skips a repost, but the claim goes further than the loop test proves.
- `docs/running.md:50` · 'The skill never returns an empty list' reads as a guarantee. The same claim is in agents/redline-reviewer.md:30, the workflow comment at line 1152 and the PR description. Yet line 54 handles an empty array on purpose, and round 1's For the person noted that a round-1 [] ends the run with no discovery pass. Saying 'has not returned an empty list in any run so far' would fit both.
- `workflows/redline-loop.js:1203` · The fence pattern needs a lowercase ```json opener on its own line. A ```JSON opener, a bare ``` or an opener with extra text after it stops the round as recipe drift, with the Claude Code version message. This has not been seen in any run; matching the opener case-insensitively would be a cheap hardening.
- `scripts/redline-guard.sh:1076` · The PR description still says nothing under scripts/ changed, but a70c243 narrowed the guard here, along with its docs and tsv rows. No spec plan in the PR names this change, since the R2-5 decision in round 2 left it for a person to make after the run.

Each finding has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the finding's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, once the round's fixes are committed.

**R4-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**Round 3's standards retrospective never landed, and its shape.md still records R3-4 as pending**

The round 3 spec ends at '## Standards retrospective (proposed)' (line 105). It proposes two edits to agent-os/standards/workflow/agents.md for R3-3 and holds a third for the R3-4 decision. Commit 6ef58a9 applied R3-3 and R3-4 (option B: a decided finding stays settled whatever its commits) but changed no standard. agents.md has no R3-3 or R3-4 text. Its coverage-pass bullet (line 35) still names `fixed` as the only reopen and says nothing about a decided finding going under For the person or a reopened finding keeping an empty knownAs. shape.md still lists R3-4 as a pending decision (line 28). It has neither the applied edits nor 'Standards retrospective: no changes'. CLAUDE.md (Specs) says a spec is not complete until its retrospective lands or that line is recorded. Task 6 step 4 of the round 3 plan (plan.md:169) planned that commit.

Proposed fix: Land the round 3 retrospective in its own commit, as the standards approver approves it. In the coverage-pass bullet of workflow/agents.md: item 1 (a reopened finding carries no knownAs, and every sentence the verifier reads states the reopen rule); item 3 as option B (a decided finding stays settled whatever its commits, and a candidate that still reproduces one goes under For the person, naming the earlier id); and item 2 if approved. Then update round 3's shape.md: Decision 4 records the person's choice of B and commit 6ef58a9. The retrospective heading records what landed, with its commit, or 'Standards retrospective: no changes' for any item declined.

**R4-2** · nit · low · confirmed

**The guard standard still says a skill fork is approved every redline-gh.sh subcommand and the narrowing is pending**

Line 23, added by this PR, says three things. A non-role session such as the coverage fork is approved 'every `redline-gh.sh` subcommand, the writes included'. tests/guard-cases.tsv pins that approval until a person narrows it. The README, docs/running.md and docs/guard.md name the narrowing as pending. Commit a70c243 landed the narrowing, so all three are now wrong. The guard approves the main group only the GH_READ subcommands (scripts/redline-guard.sh:1076). The tsv's `reply` row for a non-role session is `inert`. The three docs describe the narrowing as landed. Line 14, which this PR did not touch, still lists `redline-gh.sh` as a whole among the scripts approved for any session. The next shaper reads this standard (CLAUDE.md: work follows agent-os/standards/), so it would plan guard rows against a rule that no longer holds.

Proposed fix: Rewrite the last sentence of line 23 to match docs/guard.md: of redline-gh.sh, the fork is approved only the read subcommands. A write (a review, a reply, a comment, an issue, a thread resolve) is inert and meets the session's permission prompt (#80, R2-5; tests/guard-cases.tsv pins it). Change `redline-gh.sh` in line 14 to `redline-gh.sh`'s read subcommands. The README and docs/ need no change, since they already say this.

**R4-3** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A finding an earlier run resolved is read back as decided, so a candidate that still reproduces it can never reopen**

A run's reviewer can put a carried finding in `resolved`. resolvedReplies (line 2411) then answers its thread with `Redline round N: resolved; first reported as R3-3 in Redline round 3. <why> · decided by: redline`. In the next run, `redline-gh.sh prior-findings` strips the round prefix. Its `classify` matches none of its known prefixes, so the reply falls through to `decided` (scripts/redline-gh.sh:342). Reproduced: that classify, run with jq on this reply text, returns "decided". On every coverage round, the handled-list header (line 1126) and this sentence (line 1169) tell the verifier a decided finding stays settled whatever its commits and goes under For the person. A resolved finding is the reviewer's own claim that the code no longer has the bug, the same claim a `fixed` reply makes. The R2-1 reopen names only findings marked fixed. R3-4's reason for keeping decided findings settled (an applied decision is often a deliberate keep or mitigation) does not apply here, since nobody decided anything. Suppose the resolution was wrong, or the bug comes back. A later run's coverage pass can re-find it, and the round still confirms nothing new. The run then ends with the bug listed only under For the person. This round resolves R3-1 to R3-4, so the next run will read their threads as decided. Whether a resolved finding should reopen like a fixed one changes the done rule the person set in R2-1 and R3-4, so this is the person's call.

Proposed fix: Decision needed: should a coverage candidate that still reproduces a finding an earlier run resolved count as new, as a fixed one does? If yes: in the `classify` of `prior-findings` in scripts/redline-gh.sh, read a reply that opens with `resolved; first reported as` as `fixed`. Alternatively, add a `resolved` disposition to PRIOR_DISPOSITIONS and name it beside fixed in the handled-list header (line 1126), the reopen sentence (line 1169), agents/redline-reviewer.md and the prior-findings paragraph of docs/running.md. Either way, add a tests/gh-test.sh prior-findings case for the resolved reply and a loop-test check. If no: say in the same sentences and in docs/running.md that a finding an earlier run resolved is read as decided and stays settled.

This needs a decision from the author; Redline does not decide it.
